page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

For storage-heavy operations, the server includes a 1229 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark testing, the E32ds_v4 demonstrates solid performance across memory and compute tasks. It achieved a strong Passmark memory score of 2817.92, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 1663.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 107.55 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Multi-core stress-ng performance reached 29820.32, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered at 127.55 GB/sec.

Database and web serving benchmarks show a static web serving throughput of 21.6 GB/sec and 27.54 million operations per second for Redis SET operations. However, the system exhibits limitations in large-scale machine learning tasks; while it handles small 135M LLM inference at 195.94 text generation tokens per second, large 70B LLM prompt processing drops to a weak 5.59 tokens per second. This profile makes the E32ds_v4 highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, and caching layers, while being less suitable for heavy LLM inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure E32ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv4 family, powered by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB of memory per core, alongside a 1229 GB local SSD with Premium Storage capabilities. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong memory performance, as evidenced by a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and a small-block read bandwidth of 1663.39 GB/sec. While it excels in memory-intensive tasks, database operations, and web serving, its lack of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale AI workloads, with 70B LLM prompt processing performing weakly at 5.59 tokens per second. It is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching, and data-dense enterprise workloads.
